2.en: The Emperor’s realm is glorious in its expanse and power, united in faith, maintained by the might of its armies and the blood shed by its devoted servants. Wherever the Emperor’s gaze falls, the Imperium is renewed, scoured clean of any tarnish and made afresh in His image. And yet, there are places where the Emperor’s sight cannot reach, warrens of darkness and despair where heresy festers, the loyal suffer, and the vile go unpunished for the crimes. This is as true of the Macharian Sector as it is of any region of the galaxy, and so is the work of the Inquisition set before them — to venture into the darkness and bring with them the Emperor’s cleansing light.

6.en: What follows is a selection of Threats to the Macharian Sector worthy of the Inquisition’s wrath. These may serve as useful inclusions for an ongoing adventure or the makings of an entire campaign by themselves. See @UUID[.mgChhx2XpCIhnlea#using-threats-in-your-game]{Using Threats in Your Game} for further advice on using Threats in your game.

10.en: Each Threat featured in this chapter presents the following information:

22.en: : Covering the Threat’s general backstory, where they might operate in the sector, and most importantly, what they seek to achieve

34.en: : The powers, influence or forces the Threat has on hand to achieve their goals

46.en: : The typical means of how they go about achieving their goals

58.en: : The secrets that could unravel the Threat’s plans, what could give the players the upper hand in combatting them

66.en: Stat-blocks related to each threat are included with their entry, in the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.sNyhdSHdHgyUGSgi]{Appendix}, or found in the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ]{Bestiary}. Each Threat’s area of operations has been designed to be flexible, so you may move them to wherever you wish to suit your campaign simply by changing the named locations mentioned throughout their text.

208.en: You may use these Threats in several ways. Each is flexible enough to serve as the primary antagonist for a campaign arc, or may be used as an effective thorn in the party’s side to be purged once greater threats have been addressed. If you wish, you may simply find the stat-blocks useful game aids and craft Threats of your own, tailored to your party's interests and goals.

212.en: It is best to begin seeding rumours of these Threats into your ongoing adventures prior to their actual apperance, building their presence in the background. These rumours could be mentioned by the characters' @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.2TukBjlkS5RG5Qka.JournalEntryPage.cRcDNREGRQvZvuPl]{Contacts} or seeded during their downtime as background chatter. The Inquisition receives requests for aid and investigation from every corner of the Imperium, and rumours of these Threats may appear as part of this near-endless stream of data, attached to intelligence reports or merely mentioned in passing by other acolytes. Regardless, it will always be more satisfying for players to encounter a threat that has been seeded to some degree before they ultimately appear. This will also help to make your campaign feel smoother and more well-connected.

216.en: When the time is right, you may reveal the Threat as directly as you wish. They may emerge as part of another adventure, a threat that complicates the primary investigation. Alternatively, the characters’ Patron may simply assign their acolytes to deal with the Threat. Threats can be used as a simple and direct setup for one-shot investigations, the next step in a more extensive planned campaign, or as exciting fuel for a Patron’s @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.aKUb1Ces1eXXDUo3]{Sidereal Quests} Liability.

220.en: On a grander scale, you can weave any Threat into the fabric of your campaign. They could act as a Patron’s or characters' nemesis, showing up in person at crucial turning points to throw a spanner in the works — a literal option for a Patron’s @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.Rg69Ap4KU3SM8jHK]{Nemesis} Liability. Consider why they might have crossed paths with the characters' Patron in the past and what enmity lies between them. Wait for the worst possible time for them to interfere in the Patron’s or characters' plans.

228.en: If you wish to deploy a Threat as the driving force of an entire campaign, this will require some extra work to set up. In this case, consider the following:

236.en: Do not introduce the Threat right away. Plant clues and create a thread for the characters to pull on, relating to one of the threat’s aspects. Lead them towards an inciting incident to cement the Threat as their enemy.

244.en: Ensure the Threat has plenty of ways to evade the characters' capture or avoid confrontation until the campaign’s finale — while ensuring the Threat has a consistent presence. This is a delicate balance to achieve. Consider using aspects of the Threat’s organisation (significant minions or lieutenants under their command) to confront the characters instead, or find spaces where they can interact with the Threat on even ground, where no direct conflict can occur.

252.en: Do not reveal the Threat’s true intentions until the campaign’s midpoint. Instead, allow the characters to pull on threads and discover it for themselves. Pace it out.

260.en: Consider what other forces (including other Threats) may cross the characters' path or what other situations could complicate matters for them, especially related to whatever setting they find themselves in.

272.en: By no means are these Threats Inquisition-exclusive, though it might take an Inquisitor’s resources to root them out and defeat them. Characters bound to Patrons of other Factions can stumble upon these Threats in their own adventures, becoming a problem they might have to deal with without initial Inquisition support. If you need an Inquisitor (or characters from their retinue) to aid your Patron or characters in combatting the Threat, there is a roster of sample Patrons in @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.GgyUuP4mmxygpyOG]{ Roleplaying Inquisitors} to choose from.
